sentences.text: The type species of this genus is Perijasaurus lapaz.

The holotype specimen, UCMP 37689, is a broken dorsal vertebra approximately 55 cm tall and 45 cm long. It was found on March 27, 1943, at the western flank of the Serranía del Perijá mountain range by the Tropical Oil Company.

Rincón et al. (2022) classified Perijasaurus as a basal eusauropod belonging to the unranked family Eusauropoda. They determined it is closely related to Cetiosaurus, Patagosaurus, Bagualia, Nebulasaurus, and Spinophorosaurus.

Perijasaurus lived around 175 million years ago during the Toarcian-Aalenian boundary of the early to middle Jurassic. Its fossils come from the La Quinta Formation in what is now northern Colombia and Venezuela. The environment where it lived is interpreted as a tropical lowland forest.
The time range for the animal is the Toarcian to Aalenian, from 180.4 to 170.9 million years ago.
